title: Truth-tellers, liars and contradiction
transcript: In a truth-teller puzzle, a person's type agrees with the truth of their statement. A truth-teller's statement is true, and a liar's statement is false. Turn each sentence into a short condition. Then combine the conditions before assigning everyone's type.

AMC logic practice can ask who made a correct statement or which claims can all hold at once. Keep a small table of cases. A Rossmoyne style argument may need to rule out every alternative. Use a contradiction if some proposed assignment cannot fit its own statements.
Everyone in a puzzle is either always truthful or always lies. Ava says: I am a liar. Can Ava say that consistently? Check what would happen under each of the two possible types.
If Ava is truthful, the claim of being a liar is false. That type cannot make the statement. If Ava is a liar, the claim is true. That also contradicts the type. Neither case works.
Two people are each truthful or a liar. Ben says that both of them are liars. Work out the types of both people. The second person makes no statement. Can the first claim its own type consistently?

If Ben were truthful, both would be liars by the statement. That contradicts the idea that Ben is truthful. The claim must be false. Since Ben really is a liar, the other person has to be truthful to make the pair different.
Ava says Ben is a liar. Ben says Chen is truthful. Chen says Dara is truthful. Dara says that Ava and Chen are different types. Everyone is either always truthful or always lies. Who is truthful?

A claim that someone is truthful makes the two types match. A claim that they lie makes the types opposite. Follow the first two links from Ava to Chen. Those two links make Ava and Chen opposite types. This determines the final statement without guessing any individual type. The statement by Dara is true. So Dara is truthful.

Now use the statement about Dara to identify Chen, which is truthful. Then Ben is truthful and Ava is a liar. Check each sentence with that assignment. The last statement fixed one type, and each link then forced the next, proving there is only one assignment.

A liar's entire stated sentence must be false. When the sentence says both people lie, one truthful person is enough to make it false. Checking one person's statement is a start. All statements must agree with the proposed types at the same time.

Mark each statement as a condition. Decide whether it gives same types, opposite types, or another relationship. Look for a type forced by several conditions. Then check the remaining assignments against all the statements.
